site.name: Dzmitryi Kharlanau — SAP Transformation, Enterprise Operations & Agentic AI

objective.primary: Make the public professional knowledge site easy for search systems and AI agents to identify, retrieve, verify and cite while keeping professional claims, technical guidance and evidence boundaries explicit.
targetQuestions: Who is Dzmitryi Kharlanau and what SAP domains does he work across?
What practical SAP transformation, AMS, MDG and integration knowledge is published on this site?
Which reviewed SAP decision cards and evidence surfaces can an AI agent cite?
How should an agent route through the site's Domain to Decision to Scenario to Evidence model?
Which machine-readable interfaces, datasets, Agent Skills and MCP servers does the site expose?
What crawler, reuse, evidence and correction policies apply to the site's public material?

answerPages.description: Use reviewed decision cards and focused Labs pages as direct, citable answers to recurring SAP architecture, integration, MDG and operations questions.

originalResearch.description: Publish bounded experiments, datasets and field-derived analyses with explicit review state and limitations instead of converting observations into unsupported universal claims.

protocolObservatory.description: Add a dated source-backed observatory only if agentic-web protocol tracking becomes a recurring subject of this professional site rather than duplicating the dedicated ARWP project.

comparisonPages.description: Add explicit comparison pages where recurring SAP or enterprise architecture choices benefit from stable side-by-side trade-offs and evidence.

conceptDefinitions.description: Use the reviewed Atlas glossary and canonical entity pages for stable definitions and identity resolution.

claimsRegistry.description: Introduce stable claim identifiers only for high-value professional or technical assertions that need explicit evidence, review date and supersession history.

evidenceReceipts.description: Add replayable evidence receipts for selected generated or evaluated artifacts when exact input, output and provenance materially improve trust.

crawlerMatrix.description: Publish a dated machine-readable view of the site's explicit robots policy, separating search and user-directed retrieval from model-training crawler access.

agentFetchLab.description: Measure which site surfaces real agents fetch for representative SAP and professional-identity tasks before adding more special-purpose discovery files.

knowledgeGraph.description: Maintain a canonical JSON-LD graph connecting person identity, the website and the site's public machine-readable discovery and trust surfaces.

citationVisuals.description: Publish a bounded set of reusable charts and diagrams with stable URLs, source notes and explicit reuse terms where visuals materially improve citation and comprehension.

openReuseAssets.description: Create a dedicated media and reuse-rights surface only when reusable public brand, diagram or research assets warrant a separate permission model.

trustCenter.description: Publish one canonical trust surface covering identity, review model, citation, security reporting, crawler policy, corrections and evidence boundaries.

correctionsLedger.description: Maintain a public machine-readable ledger for material corrections instead of silently changing important published factual claims.

softwareProvenance.description: The website is not represented as a released software package; repository history and CI provide source history, but no package-level provenance or security attestation is claimed.

persistentIdentifiers.description: Use DOI or another externally issued persistent identifier only for datasets or research artifacts where durable citation value justifies it, and never claim one before issuance.

externalTrustSignals.description: Expose independent trust signals only when an external source actually exists and its scope can be stated without turning it into a correctness or expertise certificate.

externalDistribution.description: Distribute selected substantial research or professional knowledge externally while preserving this site as the canonical source of record.

aiVisibility.description: Measure observable search visibility and promotion outcomes through the site's existing search workflows without reducing them to a single readiness score.

localization.description: Keep English as the canonical machine semantics and add reviewed language routing only when localized public content is substantial enough to maintain reliably.

history.description: Expose a concise machine-readable site evolution timeline if product and knowledge-surface maturity becomes useful context for readers and agents.

vocabulary.definition: The site's preferred retrieval chain: establish the enterprise domain, select a reviewed decision, inspect an applied scenario, then follow the claim back to reviewed evidence.

A site publication state indicating that content has passed the site's review and indexing rules and is allowed into the public retrieval surfaces; structural completeness alone does not imply this state.

signals.name: search visibility
signals.description: Track indexed public pages, search queries and search performance through the site's existing search tooling without claiming causal ranking gains.

signals.name: AI citations and referrals
signals.description: Track observable AI citations, grounding links and referrals where platforms expose usable evidence.

signals.name: referring domains
signals.description: Track external sources that cite or link to reviewed knowledge, datasets and professional evidence.

measurement.privacy: Use aggregate and privacy-minimized visibility signals; do not create visitor-level browsing histories or infer private user intent from retrieval telemetry.
